Goal: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Hypothesis to revise: TITLE: Position-standardised MIL: a per-dataset normal score atlas stops MIL from selecting salient but normal anatomy
SUMMARY: Before selecting the top-k patches of abnormal images for MIL, standardise each patch's anomaly score by the mean and spread of scores at the same grid position over that dataset's normal images, so systematically high-scoring normal structures cannot be chosen as anomalies.
HYPOTHESIS: Atlas-standardised selection in asymmetric MIL reduces the fraction of selected patches that fall outside true lesions on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC training images by at least 25% and raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over unstandardised asymmetric MIL.
RATIONALE: Both parents rest on a normal reference: the position-aware bank compares a patch with normal tissue at the same location, and asymmetric MIL uses normal images as fully labelled. A different failure explains many MIL errors: some normal structures (ventricles, skull, optic disc, vessels) score high under the text anchors in every image, so top-k selection in abnormal images picks them. A positional atlas of normal scores, computed from image-labelled normal images, explains them away cheaply and needs no feature bank at all — only score statistics per position.
METHOD: 1) After each epoch, compute for each source dataset and level the per-position mean mu_uv and std sigma_uv of segmentation-branch patch anomaly probabilities over 200 random normal training images (17x17 maps). 2) In the MIL term for abnormal images, select top-k patches by (p_uv - mu_uv)/(sigma_uv + 0.05) instead of p_uv; the loss itself is still applied to p (SigLIP-style positive term). 3) Normal images keep the all-patches-normal term. 4) For datasets without spatial alignment, the atlas is replaced by a global mean/std (reduces to unstandardised selection). 5) Code: train_zero.py atlas update hook; loss.py asym_mil_loss(select_by=...).
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: asymmetric SigLIP-MIL; position-aware normal-bank pseudo-masks; mask-supervised MVFA. Ablations: atlas update frequency; global vs positional statistics. Metrics: fraction of selected patches outside true lesions (analysis on masked datasets), held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: no reduction in off-lesion selections.
